answer: One workable design: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because dawn only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, ledge is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any copper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
